newsitem.title: EL SALVADOR: Shipping line may increase American Pacific routes.
newsitem.headline: Shipping line may increase American Pacific routes.

text.p: Canadian shipper Nafta Shipping might increase routes along the American Pacific coast, the manager of El Salvador's Maritime Agency said Wednesday.
Julio Rivas told Reuters the success of the line's service, principally between Vancouver and Central America, since its launch has the company eyeing the possibility of expanding its service.

Since November, Nafta Shipping's Clipper Arita has transported more than 4,500 tonnes of cargo between Canada and the ports of Quetzal in Guatemala, Acajutla in El Salvador, Caldera in Costa Rica and Manzanillo in Mexico.
"They are thinking about bringing another ship into service so that shipments can be made every 15 days rather than every 28 days as it stands at the moment," Rivas said.
He added the line was also thinking about offering services at U.S. ports close to Long Beach and San Francisco in California.
To date, most of the cargo has been autos, malting barley, paper, other foodstuffs and construction equipment.
Nafta Shipping is part of the Clipper Group owning around 90 ships worldwide with capacities between 3,900 and 40,000 tonnes, Rivas said.
